title: Platform Manifest (v1)
description: Canonical schema for the platform.yaml file authored in service repositories. Validated by the platform pipeline and translated into the values consumed by the shared helm chart at deploy time.

apiVersion.description: Pins this manifest to v1 of the platform schema. Within v1 the schema evolves additively (new optional fields, non-breaking defaults). Breaking changes ship as a new major (v2) and require an explicit bump.

name.description: The service / app name. Convention: matches the repository name. Lowercase, hyphen-separated.

product.description: The product line this service belongs to. A coarse organisational grouping that spans many services and is independent of the owning team. Propagated to runtime pod labels for cost attribution and high-level grouping.

owner.description: The owning team's identifier — typically the GitHub team slug. Propagated to runtime pod labels so observability and cost-attribution tooling can group by team.

type.description: The type of workload. Determines which sub-pipeline and helm chart variant the platform applies.

priorityClass.description: Optional. The priority class for this workload. Omit unless the legacy config explicitly sets one — let platform defaults apply otherwise. The renderer appends `-priority` before passing to the helm chart (e.g. `critical` becomes `critical-priority`); a future chart update will adopt these shorter names directly.

replicas.description: Desired number of pod replicas in PRODUCTION. Range is 0..15 inclusive — matches the helm chart's `>=0 & <16` constraint. `0` parks the workload (no pods); auto-wake on traffic requires KEDA or equivalent and is not implied by setting `0` here. dev and staging replica counts are defaulted by the platform — do not set them here.

dependencies.description: Optional. Other services this service depends on, listed by canonical service identifier. Sort alphabetically.

Compute.description: Paired requests / limits for the PRODUCTION workload. dev and staging compute is defaulted by the platform — do not set it here.

memory.description: Kubernetes memory quantity. Must be a positive integer followed by `Mi` or `Gi`, e.g. "512Mi", "3000Mi", "2Gi".

cpu.description: Kubernetes CPU quantity in millicores. Must be a positive integer followed by `m`, e.g. "500m", "4000m". Whole cores are expressed in millicores: 2 cores is "2000m", not "2".

Environments.description: Per-environment configuration. Every block (`dev`, `staging`, `prod`, `all`) is optional — emit only the blocks the service actually needs and never emit empty stubs. Runtime semantics: `variables` are merged key-by-key with per-env values winning over `all`; `secrets` are set-unioned across `all` and the per-env block. If a value is identical across every environment, declare it once in `all`.

EnvBlock.description: The uniform shape used for every environment block. Both fields are optional; include only what's needed.

secrets.description: Names of secrets the workload needs at runtime in this block. Each entry is the secret's identifier; the platform resolves it against the secret store and injects it into the runtime environment as a variable of the same name. Names must be UPPER_SNAKE_CASE (uppercase letters, digits, underscores). Sort alphabetically. Duplicates are rejected.

EnvVars.description: A bare environment-variable map. Keys must be UPPER_SNAKE_CASE (uppercase letters, digits, underscores). Values are usually strings — booleans and numbers are accepted where the consuming application expects them.

InternetExposure.description: Optional. Configures externally-facing routing for the service. Omit entirely for purely internal services — the platform creates internal access paths automatically. Sections within (`public`, `provider`) are independently opt-in.

vhost.description: Optional. Virtual host this service responds to on ALB host-based routing. Defaults to `metadata.name` if omitted.

PublicExposure.description: Public-facing exposure via CloudFlare (browser / mobile traffic). The underlying ALB is locked to CloudFlare IP ranges at the security-group level.

enabled.description: If true, the chart creates a public ingress for this service.

additionalHostnames.description: Extra hostnames this service responds to beyond the default vhost-derived host.

ProviderExposure.description: 3rd-party provider exposure. The underlying ALB is locked to provider-specific IP whitelists at the security-group level (extended per-service via the platform's provider IP whitelist).

enabled.description: If true, the chart creates a provider ingress for this service.

additionalHostnames.description: Extra hostnames this service responds to beyond the default vhost-derived host.

Overrides.description: Optional. Departures from the chart's sane defaults. Set only the fields you need to change — helm deep-merges these onto the chart's defaults, so a partial value (e.g. just `livenessProbe.timeoutSeconds`) keeps every other default in place. The property set is closed so typos in field names are caught at validation time; value shapes are intentionally loose (the helm chart rejects malformed values at template time).

portDefinitions.description: Override the default port mapping (chart default for a standard Spring service is `{actuator: 9090, http: 8080}`). Use for non-standard ports or workers without an actuator endpoint.

livenessProbe.description: Override the chart's liveness probe (Spring Actuator on 9090 by default). Helm deep-merges, so setting only `timeoutSeconds` preserves the default httpGet path and port.

readinessProbe.description: Override the chart's readiness probe (Spring Actuator on 9090 by default). Helm deep-merges as for liveness.

terminationGracePeriodSeconds.description: Override the chart's terminationGracePeriodSeconds (default 60). Pods receive SIGKILL after this many seconds if SIGTERM didn't shut them down cleanly.

prestopGracePeriodSeconds.description: Override the chart's prestopGracePeriodSeconds (default 60). Time between the prestop hook and SIGTERM during pod replacement — used to drain in-flight requests.
